Jim Seery’s

Learnt this one from my girlfriend, who learnt it from sessions in various pubs in south Down. I have no idea who Jim Seery was, but this tune is also known as “the red haired lass”.

third tune of the live at matt molloys track on chieftains water from the well album

Jim Seery’s

This was very popular when I was in Cork last summer, however it was usually played in the key of A, which is now my preference.

Re: The Red-Haired Lass

On their album Portland, Kevin Burke recorded a wholly hexatonic version of this tune.
It is very close to the A versions already posted but has no G in it (no 7th).
It also has some trade mark Kevin Burke syncopation (a sprinkling!)
It can be heard from 3’41" here
https://youtu.be/PeOEQopVafg?t=223

X:10
A/B/AcB ABcB|ABcA BFF/F/F|EABA ABce|faec dBcB|
A2A(A A)BcB|ABcA BFF/F/F|EABA ABce|afec A2cd||
e/e/eae feaf|eaec d2cd|e/e/eae fefa|afec d2cd|
e/e/eae feaf|eaec d2cB|BccB cefa|afec dBcB||

It is the very last tune of the set and the very last tune (Tr.9.4. on the CD) on the album, ending it on a high note. Kevin plays it without any repeats twice and only repeats the first part (EABA ABce|afec A4||A2cB ABcB| etc) the last time around. Ending the set with a light, suspended ‘note’ or feeling.

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on August 16th, 2023.
